title: Gaza/Hamas
capsule: Hamas (Harakat al-Muqawama al-Islamiyya) seized full administrative control of the Gaza Strip in June 2007 after routing Fatah forces in a brief civil conflict, establishing a de facto governing authority separate from the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank. The territory — roughly 365 km² on the eastern Mediterranean coast — was subjected to an Israeli and Egyptian blockade from 2007 and experienced four major Israeli military operations (2008–9, 2012, 2014, 2021) before the October 2023 Hamas assault on Israel triggered a large-scale Israeli ground campaign that by 2025 had displaced the majority of Gaza's population and dismantled most Hamas governance infrastructure. Yahya Sinwar, who became Hamas's supreme leader in 2017 and was the principal planner of the October 7 attack, was killed by Israeli forces in October 2024.
